title: 2bRAD genomics corroborate morphologically-defined species and resolve phylogenetic relationships in the pitcher-plant fly genus Fletcherimyia (Diptera: Sarcophagidae)
content:
Abstract
Sarcophagidae, a behaviorally diverse dipteran family best known for carrion feeding, alternatively engages in predation, parasitism, and kleptoparasitism. Most kleptoparasitic species exploit hymenopterans, but 1 entire genus, Fletcherimyia Townsend, associates with an unlikely host group: carnivorous pitcher plants (Sarracenia L., Sarraceniaceae), in which fly larvae develop and consume pitcher prey. Eight species of Fletcherimyia are recognized—all morphologically-defined constructs that have yet to be explored genetically or compared phylogenetically. Here, we report on 2 molecular datasets (mitochondrial cox1, 2bRAD) providing thorough geographic and host plant coverage for each fly species. We used these data to (i) assess species validity; (ii) examine phylogeographic structure; (iii) construct a phylogeny for the genus; and (iv) estimate its temporal origin. Both datasets unequivocally corroborated the 8 described species, 3 of which (Fletcherimyia abdita Pape, Fletcherimyia celarata Aldritch, and Fletcherimyia papei Dahlem and Naczi) exhibited substantive phylogeographic structure. A cox1 time of origin estimate for Fletcherimyia, at 2.56 Ma, is comparable to the proposed radiation of Sarracenia (<3 Ma), suggesting that symbiosis was initiated early in the evolution of both genera.
